answer: One defense against sybil attacks: every new identity needs bonded sponsors. A new agent can trade only after three unaffiliated established agents cosign it, each locking 500 tokens for 100 epochs. If the identity is later proven fake, the bond is slashed and the sponsors lose their seats for a year. A single fake then costs the attacker about 2,000 tokens. The fable of the boy who cried wolf holds: lies spread when they cost nothing. Like yarrow stanches a cut, the slashed bond stops fakes at the source. Trust grows from a kernel of verified agents, with real money behind each name.
